result.summary: Independently re-ran on feature/WF02-REQ060-20260819 (commit 96b6287). `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`: clean, zero output. `LETFLOW_DEV_DB_CONFIRMED=1 mix test` (full suite, foreground/background re-run, not copied from TEST-RUNNER): 'Finished in 153.2 seconds (6.4s async, 146.7s sync) / 5 properties, 1090 tests, 0 failures' -- matches TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 claim independently. Also ran the scoped file directly: `mix test test/letflow/engine/pin_rebind_test.exs` -> '17 tests, 0 failures'. All 6 REQ-060 acceptance criteria re-checked against lib/letflow/engine/pin_rebind.ex and test/letflow/engine/pin_rebind_test.exs: AC1 (exactly one INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND event, ref/prior_version/new_version/actor/reason payload, no-op entries omitted) -- append_pins_rebound_event/6 (pin_rebind.ex:444-472) builds payload from compute_changed_entries/1 (M5, lines 424-435) which filters entries whose version already matches; confirmed by PinRebindTest 'AC1' describe block (lines 205-266), both the single-changed-entry case (payload assertion at line 236) and the no-op-entry-still-commits-one-event case (line 250). AC2 (UnknownPinRef rejects the WHOLE request, zero writes, verified via effective-pin-set readback) -- resolve_entries_against_effective_pins/2 (lines 407-419) uses Enum.reduce_while so the first unresolvable ref halts before any Multi.run(:event,...) step runs, all inside one Ecto.Multi/Repo.transaction (lines 330-357) so a mid-request halt rolls back everything; confirmed by the AC2 test (lines 272-297) which orders a valid entry BEFORE the unknown one and reads PinResolver.reconstruct_effective_pins/2 back to assert v1 (unchanged) plus zero pins_rebound_events. AC3 (COMPLETED/CANCELLED/ERROR each rejected with distinct InstanceNotRebindable, ERROR included) -- check_rebind_eligibility/1 (lines 392-399) matches status in [:completed, :cancelled, :error] deliberately NOT calling InstanceProjection.terminal?/1 (which excludes :error, confirmed instance_projection.ex terminal?/1 scope); confirmed by three separate AC3 tests (lines 305-369), each individually driving an instance to COMPLETED (auto-complete graph), CANCELLED (Engine.cancel_instance/3) and ERROR (Engine.set_instance_error/2) and asserting the exact {:instance_not_rebindable, status} tuple per status. AC4 (missing/empty reason, empty entries, malformed entry each distinct) -- fetch_reason/1 returns :invalid_reason (lines 206-217), fetch_entries/1 returns :empty_entries (lines 221-226), normalize_entry/2 returns {:malformed_entry, index, reason} (lines 246-315) -- three structurally distinct error shapes, not overlapping atoms; confirmed by 6 AC4 tests (lines 384-434) covering missing :reason key, whitespace-only reason, missing :entries key, empty entries list, missing-key malformed entry, and invalid-kind malformed entry, each asserting its own distinct shape. AC5 (effective pin set reflects new versions; reconstruction derives same set from INSTANCE_STARTED + INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND alone, no catalog read) -- confirmed via three AC5 tests (lines 442-528): reconstruct_effective_pins/2 shows v2 post-rebind (line 442), a hand-merge of INSTANCE_STARTED.pinned_versions + all INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND payloads via PinResolver.merge_effective_pins/2 matches reconstruct_effective_pins/2's own output byte-for-byte (line 463), and a structural/behavioral no-catalog-read proof: rebind_attrs() has no pin_lookup field, and a caller-supplied pin_lookup function is asserted never invoked (Agent counter stays 0, line 497). AC6 (NOWAIT lock contention -> distinct ConcurrentModification, not blocking; moduledoc states ERROR is the terminal status PIN-05's FAILED text means) -- lock_projection_nowait/3 (lines 369-386) issues `lock("FOR UPDATE NOWAIT")` and rescues only %Postgrex.Error{postgres: %{code: :lock_not_available}}, re-raising anything else; confirmed by the two-connection real-race AC6 test (lines 578-612) which holds a genuine blocking FOR UPDATE lock on a second Task/connection and asserts {:error, {:concurrent_modification, id}} returned in well under 2s (not the 5s block/timeout budget), plus row/log unchanged. The moduledoc-content test (lines 614-623) uses Code.fetch_docs/1 to assert the exact 'FAILED'/'ERROR'/'terminal for rebind purposes specifically' language is present verbatim in the shipped moduledoc, not merely eyeballed. Design-doc spot check (3 non-trivial claims, re-verified against shipped code, not trusted from REVIEWER's earlier pass): (1) all-or-nothing Multi short-circuit -- confirmed run_rebind_pins/7 (lines 321-358) chains Multi.run steps in strict dependency order (lock -> eligibility -> effective_pins -> resolved_entries -> changed_entries -> event) inside ONE Repo.transaction/1 call; Ecto.Multi's own semantics abort the whole transaction on any step's {:error, _} return, so a mid-list UnknownPinRef genuinely rolls back a lock already held and any prior in-memory validation, not just skips the append -- matches design doc section 4's 'one Ecto.Multi' claim exactly, no separate manual rollback logic needed or present. (2) three-way terminal-status check deliberately not reusing terminal?/1 -- confirmed check_rebind_eligibility/1 (lines 392-399) pattern-matches status literally, with an explicit code comment citing InstanceProjection.terminal?/1's excluded :error scope as the reason it is NOT called; grep of pin_rebind.ex confirms InstanceProjection.terminal?/1 is never referenced anywhere in the file. (3) NOWAIT lock convention ported from Reconstruction.write_back/3's lock_projection_nowait/2, not cancel_instance/3's blocking convention -- confirmed reconstruction.ex:706-720 has the identical `lock("FOR UPDATE NOWAIT")` + rescue-on-:lock_not_available shape pin_rebind.ex:369-386 ports, and engine.ex's cancel_instance/3 uses plain blocking `lock("FOR UPDATE")` (grepped, no NOWAIT there) -- design doc's claimed provenance and the deliberate convention divergence both hold. Also confirmed PinRebind never calls Registry.register_type/2 for INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND (grepped pin_rebind.ex -- zero occurrences of register_type), matching the moduledoc's stated caller-responsibility claim and the TASK_COMPLETED/INSTANCE_CANCELLED precedent, not the INSTANCE_STARTED auto-seed precedent.
